title: Xanthe and the Escarpment
premise: Beatrix Brightwater, a mountain guide erased from two nations' registries for a rescue that went wrong, is scraping a living on the fringes of the Karst Escarpment when the river floods and delivers a sealed chest bearing the crest of Vellmark, a country that no longer exists. Inside are documents proving the annexation of Vellmark was engineered through forged treaties, along with a map to a hidden archive in the high passes. Hunted by the consortium whose legitimacy the chest destroys, Beatrix must lead a small band of Vellish exiles across the range before the snows close, choosing at last between permanent invisibility and a public reckoning. They reach the archive and expose the truth, trading their anonymity for a place among people who finally know their whole story.
about_author: Astrid Galloway is the pen name of a former alpine rescue volunteer who now writes adventure fiction from a cabin above the tree line. Their novels are known for unforgiving landscapes, morally complicated heroes, and weather treated as an antagonist.

chapters.title: The River Gives Up Its Dead
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. After a spring flood, Beatrix drags a waterlogged chest from the shallows while guiding a smuggler's cargo over the low passes. The Vellmark seal stops them cold; they nearly push it back into the current. Emotional beat: the reflex to stay invisible warring with curiosity they can't kill.

chapters.title: What the Chest Would Not Say
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. In a rented loft, Beatrix pries the lock and finds forged treaty drafts and a cipher-keyed map fragment. A neighbor notices too much. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve as Beatrix realizes the papers name the rescuers who were scapegoated years ago.

chapters.title: Two Countries' Worth of Enemies
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Flashbacks interleave with the present as Beatrix recalls the botched glacier rescue that got them blacklisted, then spots consortium watchers in town. Emotional beat: grief revisited, and the first admission that running was never the same as being free.

chapters.title: The Exile at the Ferry
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Venn, an old Vellish archivist living under a false name. She recognizes the map fragment's notation and confronts Beatrix at the river ferry, offering help and demanding the chest. Emotional beat: two people built for hiding recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Terms of Passage
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Negotiation in Ilsa's back room: Ilsa brings three exiles and knowledge of the archive; Beatrix brings the only route over the Escarpment before snowfall. Emotional beat: reluctant trust, sealed not with friendship but with shared enemies.

chapters.title: The Company of Strangers
chapters.summary: POV Tomas Rell, youngest exile, a forger's son who idolizes Beatrix's outlaw legend. The party sets out; personalities grate on the first climb. Emotional beat: the fragile comedy of strangers becoming a rope team.

chapters.title: First Blood on the Scree
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Consortium riders ambush them at the scree fields; Beatrix's route-reading saves the group but a guide's trick nearly kills a rider. Emotional beat: Beatrix confronting how much of their skill was honed for escape rather than care.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Venn. Around the fire, Ilsa admits she helped authenticate one of the forged treaties decades ago, believing she was preserving peace. Emotional beat: guilt offered honestly, and the group deciding justice matters more than purity.

chapters.title: The Pass That Isn't on Maps
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix leads them up a route known only to blacklisted guides, a smugglers' corridor erased from every official chart. Emotional beat: pride in the knowledge that illegitimacy taught them, and a flicker of belonging among the erased.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: POV Tomas Rell. The barometer falls; snows are coming early. A supply cache they counted on has been burned by consortium scouts ahead of them. Emotional beat: fear turning the group's bickering into something like loyalty.

chapters.title: The Widow of High Camp
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. They shelter with Maren, a herder widow who once guided with Beatrix's disgraced mentor. She feeds them, warns them the consortium has doubled its bounty, and refuses payment. Emotional beat: proof that kindness survives outside the law.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Col
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Venn. One exile, Davor, has been feeding their position to the consortium since the ferry; he takes the map fragment and descends toward the riders. Emotional beat: betrayal landing hardest on Ilsa, who vouched for him.

chapters.title: Chase Down the Icefall
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Beatrix and Tomas pursue Davor across the icefall; a serac collapse kills Davor and nearly takes Tomas, but the map fragment is lost with him. Emotional beat: victory that feels like failure, and Beatrix carrying a survivor out again.

chapters.title: Reading the Cipher by Starlight
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Venn. Without the fragment, Ilsa reconstructs the archive's location from memory and the treaty drafts' marginalia. Emotional beat: scholarship as courage, and the group recommitting with nothing left to trade but themselves.

chapters.title: The Consortium Closes the Valley
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. From a ridge, they watch riders seal the southern valleys; the only way out is forward, higher, into weather no sane guide would enter. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into the calm Beatrix wears like armor.

chapters.title: White Silence
chapters.summary: POV Tomas Rell. The storm hits. Rope work, whiteout, a night buried in a snow cave where Tomas breaks down and Beatrix tells the true story of the glacier rescue at last. Emotional beat: confession as shelter.

chapters.title: The Door Under the Glacier
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Storm-broken but alive, they find the archive mouth behind the glacier's retreat, exactly where the mentor's old notes said it would be. Emotional beat: awe, and the sense of walking into the past's open hand.

chapters.title: The Vellmark Archive
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Venn. Inside: original treaties, ledgers of bribes, and names, including the consortium's founders and the officials who blacklisted Beatrix. Emotional beat: vindication arriving cold and heavy, less sweet than imagined.

chapters.title: Riders at the Moraine
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The consortium's lead hunter, Corvane, corners them at the moraine with the passes closed behind everyone. Beatrix offers a guide's bargain: safe conduct down, or the mountain decides for all of them. Emotional beat: nerve held against arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Descent Nobody Owns
chapters.summary: POV Tomas Rell. Corvane's own men, unwilling to die for forged paper, force his hand; the party leads a mixed column down the ice in deteriorating light. Emotional beat: authority earned by competence, not law.

chapters.title: Testimony in the Low Town
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Venn. In the valley town, the documents go out by courier, press, and pulpit faster than the consortium can burn them; hearings are demanded in three capitals. Emotional beat: the quiet thunder of truth going public.

chapters.title: A Name on the Register
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Spring comes. Beatrix's blacklist is struck, and a new guide service opens under their own name, staffed by exiles and taught to anyone the mountains will have. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not granted, and the range finally feeling like home.
